Types of Cases Heard in the Pittsylvania County Court

Civil Cases

Traffic Cases

Traffic cases are heard in the Pittsylvania County Court and involve individuals who have been charged with a traffic violation. These cases can include speeding tickets, reckless driving, and other types of traffic offenses.

Juvenile Cases

Juvenile cases are heard in the Pittsylvania County Court and involve individuals under the age of 18 who have been charged with a crime. These cases are handled differently than adult criminal cases and are designed to provide minors with a second chance and help them stay on the right track.

Domestic Relations Cases

Domestic relations cases are heard in the Pittsylvania County Court and involve disputes between individuals who are in a domestic relationship, such as married couples, partners, or family members. These cases can include divorce, child custody, and support disputes.

Court Proceedings in Pittsylvania County

A pretrial conference is a meeting between the judge, the prosecution, and the defense to discuss the details of the case and determine the best course of action. During this conference, the parties may discuss potential plea bargains or strategies for moving forward with the case.

Trial

The trial is the main event in a court case, where the evidence and testimony are presented to the jury. During the trial, the judge oversees the proceedings and ensures that the law is followed.

Sentencing

If an individual is found guilty, the judge will determine the appropriate sentence, which can include fines, imprisonment, or other penalties. The judge will take into account the specifics of the case, the defendant's criminal history, and other relevant factors when determining the sentence.

Appeal

If an individual is not satisfied with the outcome of their case, they may have the right to appeal the decision to a higher court. The appeal process is a complex and technical process that requires the services of an experienced attorney.
